item.content:encoded:
+A couple grammatical errors, nothing major
– hide block

He found himself half-buried in the sand and attempted to move, but too weak to do so.

There's a missing phrase or set of words between "but" and "too weak"; you could put "was", "found himself", or something else to make it read correctly.

His body parts, barely holding together, each anguished fragment emitted a chorus of screams.

I think there should be a comma after "fragment", but I may be wrong.

Vaguely, he would recall a war.

"Could" would fit better than "would" here, and it would work better with the previous few lines.


Overall, I think this piece is pretty solid. The prose and narration are descriptive and evocative without being too purple, and the characterization of the Broken God is definitely interesting. I've seen the BG depicted as a terrifying, ever-growing anomaly that enslaves people and turns them into insane cultists, and I've seen Him depicted as a valiant combatant in the war against the true evil, The Flesh. But I've never seen him depicted as a helpless, confused victim, and I think this pulls that off very well. It really capitalizes the "broken" aspect of the Broken God, and I think that's an aspect of Him that doesn't get as much attention as it should. +1 for originality, a compelling narrative and awesome art.

It was when the waves splashed against his body that he gradually returned to consciousness. How long had he been lying here? He found himself half-buried in the sand and attempted to move, but too weak to do so.

This is quite literally the beginning of Inception, so I pictured a human (Leonardo DiCaprio, actually) for all of it. However, now that I see the tags and author post, I'm definitely upvoting. Unique and artistic, this one.

item.content:encoded:
Bascially, Broken God has feelings, be nice to it :3 (The picture is a link~)

Huge thanks to Metaphysician and Vezaz~

But no this is not an attempt to humanize Broken God, it does not think in human terms. I merely want to show the pain it suffers from breaking apart. I always think the reason behind such Broken God skips' tendency to turn other things into clockwork, is because they no longer fuction properly, and can not "think" and perceive things in the way they should. They suffer huge pain, and will try to get everything in their grip to make up for the missing parts.
